Are you ready for what’s next?

Come explore opportunities within Brunswick, a global marine leader committed to challenging conventions and innovating next-generation technologies that transform experiences on the water and beyond. Brunswick believes “Next Never Rests™,” and we offer a variety of exciting careers and growth opportunities within united teams defining the future of marine recreation.

Mercury Marine- Fond Du Lac, WI- Advanced Manufacturing team / Global Operations Excellence Co-op

Location: Plant 17- Fond du Lac, WI

Workplace Category: Onsite

Travel Required: No

Direct Reports: No

Pay Range: $18.00-27.50

Visa Sponsorship: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Relocation: Yes

Innovation is the heart of Brunswick. See how your contributions will help transform vision into reality:

Position Overview:

As part of the talented Advanced Manufacturing team / Global Operations Excellence division, you will get to work on:

- CAD Modeling, Simulation, 3D Printing

- ETL/Data Analytics and BI tools

- Robotics and Automation

This position will be integral in supporting manufacturing engineering technologies across different operational plants. Candidate needs to be self-starter with passion for manufacturing and the ability to work on multiple projects at once.

At Brunswick, we have passion for our work and a distinct ability to deliver.

Essential Functions:

- Work with full-time team members located in multiple operational plants, assisting with projects and analysis

- Collaborate with Management, Manufacturing, Automation, Quality, and Process Engineers across the business

- Interact and program various types of automation equipment like robots, PLC's, servos

- Connect, collect, and analyze data from different types of operational equipment

- Exposure to and assist with various types of Simulation work

- Work with tools like Power BI, SQL, MS Azure Suite, CAD

In addition to a great hands-on learning experience, you will also acquire the skills needed to:

- Understand manufacturing systems and the technical problems that exist in operations

- Understand Continuous Improvement (Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen) and Connected Operations (Industry 4.0, IIoT, Machine Learning) implemented in a highly vertically integrated manufacturing environment

- Present findings and recommendations to operational management

- Interpret manufacturing prints and quality requirements

- Analyze data and make recommendations that effectively improve process costs

- Effectively express your ideas, influence people and communicate with employees at all levels of an organization (hourly and salary)

Diversity of thought and experiences is fundamental when imagining the unimaginable. Certain skillsets/experiences are necessary; however, others can be developed along the way.

Required Qualifications:

- Current enrollment in a BS program with a major in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Data Science or a relevant degree with an Engineering or Data Emphasis

- Ability to manage multiple projects at the same time

- Self-starter and highly motivated to learn

- Minimum second semester sophomore status with 48 completed credits

- Availability to work full-time (40 or more hours per week) through a full co-op term running May to December 2027

- Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs

- Permanent US Work Authorization required

Working Conditions:

- Learning Opportunities: Our Student Program is designed to provide hands-on experience in a professional setting. You will work alongside experienced professionals and get a chance to apply your academic knowledge to real-world tasks.

- Project Work: The work environment is supportive, collaborative, and conducive to learning. Student co-ops or interns typically work on specific projects or tasks that contribute to the organization’s goals. This may range from supporting larger projects to handling smaller, individual assignments.

- Hours: Co-ops and Interns are expected to work a full 40-hour work week

- Feedback and Performance Reviews: As a co-op or intern, you will receive feedback and performance reviews throughout your assignment. We value the importance for interns to understand their progress and areas for improvement.

The anticipated pay range for this position is $18.00 - $27.50 per hour. The actual hourly rate offered will vary depending on multiple factors including year in school/credits earned, degree, job-related knowledge/skills, relevant experience, business needs, and geographic location. Compensation decisions are dependent upon the specifics of the candidate’s qualifications and the business context.

Why Brunswick:

Whatever tomorrow brings, we’ll be at the leading edge. As the clear leader in the marine industry, we’re committed to our values and supporting our exceptional people. We offer and encourage growth opportunities within and across our many brands. In addition, we’re proud of being recognized for making a splash with numerous awards!

About Mercury Marine:

Mercury Marine is a world leading manufacturer of marine propulsion systems. A $2.6 billion division of Brunswick Corporation (NYSE: BC), Mercury designs, manufactures and distributes engines, services and parts for recreational, commercial and government marine applications, empowering boaters with products that are easy to use, extremely reliable and backed by the most dedicated customer support in the world with 10,000 service points globally. Mercury’s industry-leading brand portfolio includes Mercury outboard engines; Mercury MerCruiser sterndrive and inboard packages; Mercury global parts and accessories; Land ’N’ Sea, BLA, Payne’s Marine, Kellogg Marine & Lankhorst Taselaar marine parts distribution; and Mercury and Quicksilver parts and oils. More information is available at mercurymarine.com.

Next is Now!

We value growth and development, recognizing that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying.

About Invesco

As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco.

What’s in it for you?

Our people are at the very core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our benefit and perk offerings including:

- Company networking events with other interns

- Peer Sponsor Program

- Leadership Connection series

- Virtual Lunch and Learns

- Invesco Cares volunteer events

- Complimentary coffee and snacks

- 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution

Job Description

Ready to make your mark in the world of data governance? Spend an unforgettable summer at Invesco alongside a select group of driven students. Our 9-week Summer Internship Program offers you the opportunity to work within our Corporate Functions Data Office, supporting initiatives that improve how data is governed, understood, and used across Finance, HR, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, and Risk.

As part of our Summer Internship Program cohort, you’ll participate in orientation, networking events, development workshops, and volunteer activities. You’ll work side by side with talented teams to learn about the business and contribute to meaningful initiatives that support data governance, data quality, reporting and process improvement across Corporate Functions.

If you enjoy analyzing data, improving processes, and turning information into clear insights, this role offers a unique opportunity to apply your skills in a dynamic, cross-functional environment. You’ll support initiatives that strengthen data governance, improve data quality, and help Corporate Functions use data more effectively.

Here’s the best part: crush your internship, and you could be eligible for a full-time offer to join our Early Career Program after graduation!

What You’ll Do

Support data governance initiatives across Corporate Functions:

- Help maintain inventories of critical data elements, data owners, data stewards, and key business processes

- Support preparation of materials for data governance meetings, working groups, and stakeholder updates

Assist with data quality and metadata activities:

- Analyze datasets to identify completeness, consistency, or accuracy issues

- Help document data definitions, business rules, lineage, and usage for key Corporate Function data

- Support data quality issue tracking by organizing findings, actions, owners, and status updates

Contribute to reporting, dashboards, and process improvement:

- Create or update dashboards, trackers, and summary reports to monitor data governance progress and key metrics

- Map current-state processes and help identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, or automate recurring activities

- Assist with preparing executive-ready summaries, presentations, and visual materials that communicate insights clearly

Support cross-functional projects and research:

- Research leading practices in data governance, data management, AI readiness, and regulatory expectations

- Partner with team members across Corporate Functions to gather information, validate documentation, and support project deliverables

- Assist with ad hoc projects related to data governance, data quality, master data, controls, or transformation initiatives

What You Get

- Broad Exposure to Corporate Functions Data Governance – Contribute to projects involving data governance, data quality, reporting, process improvement, and cross-functional initiatives across Corporate Functions

- Access to Finance Leadership – Connect with finance leaders throughout the summer and gain insight into how strategic decisions are made across the business

- Cross-Functional Projects & Ownership – Work on initiatives beyond your immediate team and take ownership of meaningful projects, with opportunities to see work through from concept to completion

- Career Launchpad – Build real-world skills and set the foundation for a future at Invesco and beyond

- Dedicated Mentorship – Get paired with a mentor to guide your experience and support your growth

- Intern Community – Collaborate, share ideas, and build lasting connections with fellow interns

- Pathway to Full-Time – Strong performance may lead to a full-time offer through our Early Career Program

Minimum Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program and graduating by summer of 2028

- All majors welcome, with an emphasis on Business, Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field

- Demonstrated interest in data, analytics, data governance, or process improvement

- Must be able to work in one of Invesco’s offices where the program is available

- Must be authorized to work in the U.S. on a permanent basis. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program. Invesco will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT)

- Relocation and housing will not be included if an offer is extended

Preferred Qualifications

- Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills

- Ability to organize assignments and meet deadlines

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to summarize information clearly

- Interest in data governance, data quality, metadata, reporting, or process improvement

- Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel

- Experience with or interest in data visualization, reporting, or analytics tools such as Power BI, Tableau, SQL, or similar

- Ability to work collaboratively across teams and functions

Full Time / Part Time

Full time

Worker Type

Student/Intern (Fixed Term)

Job Exempt (Yes / No)

No

Workplace Model

Pursuant to Invesco’s Workplace Policy, employees are expected to comply with the firm’s most current workplace model, which as of October 1, 2025, includes spending at least four full days each week working in an Invesco office. This reflects our belief that spending time together in the office helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more easily, and support each other’s growth and development.

The above information on this description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this role. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. The job holder may be required to perform other duties as deemed appropriate by their manager from time to time.

Invesco's culture of inclusivity and its commitment to diversity in the workplace are demonstrated through our people practices. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, citizenship status, disability, age, or veteran status. Our equal opportunity employment efforts comply with all applicable U.S. state and federal laws governing non-discrimination in employment.

CPT & Pre-Opt candidates invited to apply.

This is a paid internship; however, the intern must provide their own housing and transportation. Business related transportation and expenses will be paid by the organization. This intern will work full-time through the Summer of 2027. The internship is located in the Sun Prairie, WI office location. If pursuing internship credit through your university, it is your responsibility to consult with your advisor and review the internship's job description to ensure it meets the minimum eligibility requirements.

The contributions you will make:

The Engineering Intern is a temporary developmental role designed to provide students with practical experience building and operating modern digital solutions while developing the technical, professional, and business capabilities needed for a successful software engineering career. Working within a cross-functional product team and with close guidance from experienced engineers, this role contributes to well-defined software design, development, testing, automation, deployment, support, and improvement activities while learning how engineering work connects to product objectives, client needs, and business value. The Engineering Intern develops learning agility by actively seeking coaching, rapidly applying feedback and new knowledge, and responsibly exploring cloud-native, DevSecOps, automation, observability, AI-enabled tools and practices, Agentic AI patterns, and AI agents.

A typical day:

- Own Engineering Delivery by completing well-defined engineering assignments under guidance, with attention to quality, security, reliability, maintainability, supportability, testing, documentation, and established engineering standards.

- Develop Technical Foundations and Learning Agility by applying software engineering fundamentals while learning the team's technologies, domain concepts, and modern cloud-native, DevSecOps, automated testing, CI/CD, observability, and delivery practices.

- Demonstrates curiosity, actively seeks coaching, experiments responsibly within established guardrails, and rapidly applies feedback and new knowledge.

- Uses AI-enabled engineering tools and practices, Agentic AI patterns, and AI agents with appropriate supervision to accelerate learning and improve productivity and quality while validating results, protecting sensitive information, and maintaining human accountability.

- Connect Engineering to Business Outcomes by developing an understanding of product goals, client needs, business priorities, and how assigned engineering work contributes to team objectives and meaningful business value. Begins building a trusted, value-added partner mindset by listening to comprehend, asking thoughtful questions, offering relevant observations, and reliably following through on commitments.

- Strengthen Team Effectiveness by actively participating in Agile ceremonies, technical discussions, code reviews, testing, documentation, operational support, root-cause learning, and continuous improvement.

- Demonstrates resilience by adapting to feedback and changing priorities, learning from mistakes and setbacks, and persisting through routine technical challenges.

- Collaborate Across Teams by building productive and trusted working relationships with engineers, quality engineers, product managers, architects, platform engineers, UX designers, and business partners.

- Build Personal Capability by actively seeking coaching, reflecting on experiences, rapidly applying feedback and new knowledge, sharing learning, and demonstrating accountability for growth.

- Contributes to an inclusive, positive, and engaging environment where team members take the work seriously, enjoy working together, and recognize progress and success while preparing for potential progression into an Associate Engineer role.

The skills and experience we prefer you have:

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline.

- Completion of coursework in programming, software engineering fundamentals, algorithms, data structures, or comparable technical subjects.

- Experience developing software through academic coursework, personal projects, hackathons, research, open-source contributions, or comparable learning experiences.

- Demonstrated learning agility through curiosity, active feedback seeking, rapid application of new technical concepts, and adaptation of approaches to solve problems.

- Experience with one or more modern programming languages or development frameworks.

- Exposure to cloud-native application development concepts and one or more cloud platforms.

- Familiarity with Git-based source control and Agile software development.

- Exposure to automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, DevSecOps, or observability practices.

- Ability to develop clean, maintainable, and well-tested software while working under appropriate guidance and established engineering practices.

- Ability to analyze routine technical problems, ask effective questions, and apply foundational engineering principles to identify solutions.

- Ability to responsibly use AI-enabled engineering tools and practices, Agentic AI patterns, and AI agents with appropriate supervision while applying critical thinking, validating outputs, protecting sensitive information, maintaining human accountability, and following engineering standards.

- Ability to demonstrate learning agility by actively seeking and applying feedback, rapidly acquiring new knowledge, experimenting within appropriate guardrails, reflecting on outcomes, and continuously improving technical and professional capabilities.

- Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders; listens to comprehend, asks thoughtful questions, builds trust through reliable follow-through, and begins contributing value-added observations or ideas.

- Ability to collaborate within cross-functional product teams, incorporate feedback and diverse perspectives, and contribute to an inclusive, positive, and engaging team environment.

- Ability to organize assigned work, adapt to changing priorities, and persist through routine ambiguity, mistakes, setbacks, and technical challenges.

- Understanding of secure software development fundamentals, quality engineering principles, and the responsibility to protect confidential information and client data.

How we will take care of you:

Actual hourly rate offered is dependent upon year in school, work experience, transferable skills, business needs and market demands. The hourly rate range is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Compeer Financial is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States. Compeer is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

Thank you for considering a career with the Research Foundation of The City University of New York (RFCUNY).

The team at RFCUNY is made up of dedicated, talented professionals committed to providing the services that allow CUNY researchers, faculty, and staff to focus on their intellectual curiosity and scientific discoveries.

We are pleased that you are interested in exploring opportunities to join RFCUNY.

Primary Location:

OFFICE OF SR. UNIV DEAN FOR ACADEMIC AFFAIRS

Bargaining Unit:

No

Description

The City University of New York (CUNY) is the nation’s largest urban public university and serves 235,000 degree- seeking students and 150,000 non-degree students across 25 campuses. 77% are students of color. CUNY's core mandate is to provide a high-quality, affordable education to all New Yorkers. Guided by CUNY’s seven-year strategic plan, CUNY Lifting NY, to achieve this mission, it is imperative that CUNY students have access to high quality work‐based learning experiences that allow them to gain and demonstrate skills, experience real‐world applications, and directly launch their careers.

The CUNY Office of Careers & Industry Partnerships (OCIP) reports to the Chancellor and the University Provost and is responsible for mobilizing the university’s unparalleled scale, assets, and diverse talent to fuel inclusive economic prosperity and is dedicated to the mission of connecting academic pursuits with career competitiveness. OCIP works closely with industry to understand the skills required for the most in-demand jobs and trains City University of New York (CUNY) students in those skills to prepare them for early and sustained career success.

GENERAL DESCRIPTION

The Office of Career and Internship Programs seeks a collaborative and results-driven professional to lead and expand CUNY’s public sector internship initiatives.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Career Development and Internships, the Director will lead the development and growth of university-wide internship programs in partnership with New York City and State agencies. This role will focus on scaling employer partnerships, expanding paid internship opportunities for CUNY students, and strengthening pathways to public sector careers. The Director will work closely with campuses, government partners, and other stakeholders to align programs with workforce needs and increase access to high-quality, career-connected learning experiences.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership and Program Development

• Lead the design, expansion, and evaluation of innovative paid work-based learning initiatives aligned with institutional priorities, labor market trends, employer workforce needs, and student

success goals. • Establish program goals, performance metrics, operational standards, and annual work plans to measure program effectiveness and ensure continuous improvement.

• Provide leadership, supervision, coaching, and professional development to program managers and staff, establishing performance expectations, monitoring progress toward departmental goals, and fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and student-centered work environment.

• Develop, cultivate, and sustain strategic partnerships with government agencies, employers, academic departments, career services, faculty, campus leadership, and university administrators to integrate internships and experiential learning into academic pathways and increase student participation.

• Increase the number of employer partners through new partnerships and funding opportunities that support program growth and sustainability.

Program Operations, Administration, and Performance Management

• Direct the day-to-day administration of multiple internship and experiential learning programs, ensuring effective program delivery, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and high-quality student experiences.

• Create and manage program budgets, fiscal planning, contracts, and financial reporting, coordinating with university and external fiscal partners to ensure compliance, and adherence to grant and funding agency requirements.

• Lead the collection, analysis, and develop reporting of program data to evaluate performance, measure student and employer outcomes, assess return on investment, and identify opportunities for operational and programmatic improvement.

• Represent senior leadership in internal and external meetings as assigned, providing leadership continuity and strategic support during leadership absences.

• Perform other related duties and special projects as needed.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

• Minimum five (5) years of experience in a managerial or supervisory role

• Ability to think strategically, problem-solve, and develop programs and plans to achieve organizational goals

• Cultural competency and commitment to promoting opportunity and equity in higher education and conducting workshops, webinars, and other career readiness activities and events for students.

• Proactive, diplomatic and collaborative work style with strong supervisory, interpersonal communication, group facilitation, relationship building and presentation skills to work effectively with stakeholders.

• Dependable with effective organizational, time management and priority setting skills to manage multiple assignments and projects and meet deadlines

• Demonstrated computer skills and experience with standard desktop tools (e.g., MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint; Zoom)

• Ability to travel to multiple sites throughout NYC

• Bachelor's degree required

Preferred Qualifications

• Familiarity with CUNY, RF CUNY, CRM platforms, or student recruitment platforms (e.g, AirTable and Handshake)

• Knowledge of career development education policy issues, especially those related to college & career readiness and a deep understanding of access and equity issues

•Work Environment and Physical Requirements

• This position is based in a professional office environment and follows a hybrid work schedule: 70% in-person (7 days) and 30% remote (3 days) during each two-week payroll cycle.

• Laptops and other equipment will be provided to support working remotely.

• While performing these duties, the employee may be required to:

o Sit for extended periods

o Use a computer and other office equipment

o Occasionally lift or move items up to 20 pounds

• Reasonable accommodations will be provided to individuals with disabilities or other needs in accordance with RFCUNY policies and applicable laws.

• Ability to travel to multiple sites throughout NYC.

EEO

We are committed to enhancing our diverse academic community by actively encouraging people of any race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, disability, age, or protected veteran status to apply. We take pride in our pluralistic community and continue to seek excellence through diversity and inclusion. CUNY is an EEO/AA Employer.

Pay Range:

$115,000 - $120,000

RFCUNY Benefits
RFCUNY Employee Benefits and Accruals

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
The Research Foundation of the City University of New York is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action/Americans with Disabilities Act/E-Verify Employer. It is the policy of the Research Foundation of CUNY to provide equal employment opportunities free of discrimination based on race, color, age, religion, sex, pregnancy, childbirth, national origin, disability, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, domestic violence victim status, arrest record, criminal conviction history, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.
